relevance_note: One cohort member (Table 1 case 19) carries two ALDH5A1 variants with individual detail: "Compound heterozygous variants in ALDH5A1 were found in a female patient with ASD, epilepsy, hypotonia, developmental delay, and motor coordination deficits".
method_note: WES cohort of 22 Bulgarian ASD patients; only case 19 (ALDH5A1, Tables 1 and 2) is in scope; the other 21 cases carry variants in other genes and get no rows. Label 'Table 1 #19' from the bare-number 'Case' column; the text gives no own label. The paper never names SSADH deficiency as this patient's diagnosis; it calls her a female patient with ASD and says 'ALDH5A1 deficiency likely disrupts neurotransmitter balance'. The Discussion sentence about the ALDH5A1 female patient was linked to case 19 because she is the only ALDH5A1 carrier in Tables 1-2. Zygosity: Table 1 lists each variant as 'Heterozygous'; the Discussion calls them 'Compound heterozygous'; recorded compound heterozygous. Inheritance taken from Table 1's per-variant Inheritance column (Paternal/Maternal) after stated segregation analysis with parental DNA; the parents are not otherwise described, so they get no individual rows. 'Age of Testing (Years)' = 3 recorded as age at last evaluation (age at genetic testing; clinical examination preceded testing); no age at onset or diagnosis given. Observed intellectual disability, neuropsychological delay, poor social interaction, speech deterioration and repetitive behavior come from statements about all 22 patients (named group including her). 'movement disorders' and 'coordination problems' are unspecified, so ataxia/dystonia/dyskinesia checklist items are not reported. cites_prior_report is true only because the SPATA5 patient (case 7, out of scope) was described in ref [89]; no prior report of the ALDH5A1 patient is stated. Built with a short script from my reading; no table transcribed by script. No contradictions found beyond the zygosity wording.

span: we performed whole exome sequencing on a cohort of 22 Bulgarian male and female individuals showing ASD features alongside segregation analyses of their families
To verify the variants detected by WES, the target regions of the human genome, were multiplied by polymerase chain reaction (PCR). The amplified fragments were sequenced by Sanger’s method
The cohort of 22 patients had been examined clinically and neuropsychologically in children’s neurological and psychiatric clinics in Bulgaria prior to genetic testing
